27.8: For what hope hath the hypocrite when he hath heaped up riches, if God take away his soul?
27.9: Will God hear his cry, when trouble cometh upon him?
27.10: Will he set his delight on the Almighty? will he call upon God at all times?
27.11: I will teach you what is in the hand of God, and I will not conceal that which is with the Almighty.
27.12: Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it: why then do you thus vanish vanity?
27.13: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of tyrants, which they shall receive of the Almighty.
27.14: If his children be in great number, the sword shall destroy them, and his posterity shall not be satisfied with bread.
27.15: His remnant shall be buried in death, and his widows shall not weep.
27.16: Though he should heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay,
27.17: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.
27.18: He buildeth his house as the moth, and as a lodge that the watchman maketh.
27.19: When the rich man sleepeth, he shall not be gathered to his fathers: they opened their eyes, and he was gone.
27.20: Terrors shall take him as waters, and a tempest shall carry him away by night.
27.21: The East wind shall take him away, and he shall depart: and it shall hurl him out of his place.
27.22: And God shall cast upon him and not spare, though he would fain flee out of his hand.
27.23: Every man shall clap their hands at him, and hiss at him out of their place.

28.1: The silver surely hath his vein, and the gold his palace, where they take it.
28.2: Iron is taken out of the dust, and brass is molten out of the stone.
28.3: God putteth an end to darkness, and he trieth the perfection of all things: he setteth a bond of darkness, and of the shadow of death.
28.4: The flood breaketh out against the inhabitant, and the waters forgotten of the foot, being higher than man, are gone away.
28.5: Out of the same earth cometh bread, and under it, as it were fire is turned up.
28.6: The stones thereof are a place of Sapphires, and the dust of it is gold.
28.7: There is a path which no fowl hath known, neither hath the kite’s eye seen it.
28.8: The Lion’s whelps have not walked it, nor the Lion passed thereby.
28.9: He putteth his hand upon the rocks, and overthroweth the mountains by the roots.
28.10: He breaketh rivers in the roots, and his eye seeth every precious thing.
28.11: He bindeth the floods, that they do not overflow, and the thing that is hid, bringeth he to light.
28.12: But where is wisdom found? and where is the place of understanding?
28.13: Man knoweth not the price thereof: for it is not found in the land of the living.
28.14: The depth saith, It is not in me: the Sea also saith, It is not with me.
28.15: Gold shall not be given for it, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof.
28.16: It shall not be valued with the wedge of gold of Ophir, nor with the precious onyx, nor the sapphire.
28.17: The gold nor the crystal shall be equal unto it, nor the exchange shall be for plate of fine gold.
28.18: No mention shall be made of coral, nor of the gabish: for wisdom is more precious than pearls.
28.19: The Topaz of Ethiopia shall not be equal unto it, neither shall it be valued with the wedge of pure gold.
28.20: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding,
28.21: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all the living, and is hid from the fowls of the heaven?
28.22: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.
28.23: But God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.
28.24: For he beholdeth the ends of the world, and seeth all that is under heaven,
28.25: To make the weight of the winds and to weigh the waters by measure.
28.26: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunders,
28.27: Then did he see it, and counted it: he prepared it, and also considered it.
28.28: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord is wisdom, and to depart from evil is understanding.

29.1: So Job proceeded, and continued his parable, saying,
29.2: Oh that I were as in times past, when God preserved me!
29.3: When his light shined upon mine head: and when by his light I walked through the darkness,
29.4: As I was in the days of my youth: when God’s providence was upon my tabernacle:
29.5: When the Almighty was yet with me, and my children round about me:
29.6: when I washed my paths with butter, and when the rock poured me out rivers of oil:
29.7: When I went out to the gate, even to the judgment seat, and when I caused them to prepare my seat in the street.
29.8: The young men saw me, and hid themselves, and the aged arose, and stood up.
29.9: The princes stayed talk, and laid their hand on their mouth.
29.10: The voice of princes was hid, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.
29.11: And when the ear heard me, it blessed me, and when the eye saw me, it gave witness to me.
29.12: For I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.
29.13: The blessing of him that was ready to perish, came upon me, and I caused the widow’s heart to rejoice.
29.14: I put on justice, and it covered me: my judgment was as a robe, and a crown.
29.15: I was the eyes to the blind, and I was the feet to the lame.
29.16: I was a father unto the poor, and when I knew not the cause, I sought it out diligently.
29.17: I brake also the jaws of the unrighteous man, and plucked the prey out of his teeth.
29.18: Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply my days as the sand.
29.19: For my root is spread out by the water, and the dew shall lie upon my branch.
29.20: My glory shall renew toward me, and my bow shall be restored in mine hand.
29.21: Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and held their tongue at my counsel.
29.22: After my words they replied not, and my talk dropped upon them.
29.23: And they waited for me, as for the rain, and they opened their mouth as for the latter rain.
29.24: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: neither did they cause the light of my countenance to fall.
29.25: I appointed out their way, and did sit as chief, and dwelt as a King in the army, and like him that comforteth the mourners.

30.1: But now they that are younger than I, mock me: yea, they whose fathers I have refused to set with the dogs of my flocks.
30.2: For whereto should the strength of their hands have served me, seeing age perished in them?
30.3: For poverty and famine they were solitary, fleeing into the wilderness, which is dark, desolate and waste.
30.4: They cut up nettles by the bushes, and the juniper roots was their meat.
30.5: They were chased forth from among men: they shouted at them, as at a thief.
30.6: Therefore they dwelt in the clefts of rivers, in the holes of the earth and rocks.
30.7: They roared among the bushes, and under the thistles they gathered themselves.
30.8: They were the children of fools, and the children of villains, which were more vile than the earth.
30.9: And now am I their song, and I am their talk.
30.10: They abhor me, and flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.
30.11: Because that God hath loosed my cord and humbled me, they have loosed the bridle before me.
30.12: The youth rise up at my right hand: they have pushed my feet, and have trode on me as on the paths of their destruction.
30.13: They have destroyed my paths: they took pleasure at my calamity, they had no help.
30.14: They came as a great breach of waters, and under this calamity they come on heaps.
30.15: Fear is turned upon me: and they pursue my soul as the wind, and mine health passeth away as a cloud.
30.16: Therefore my soul is now poured out upon me, and the days of affliction have taken hold on me.
30.17: It pierceth my bones in the night, and my sinews take no rest.
30.18: For the great vehemency is my garments changed, which compasseth me about, as the collar of my coat.
30.19: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like ashes and dust.
30.20: When I cry unto thee, thou dost not hear me, neither regardest me, when I stand up.
30.21: Thou turnest thyself cruelly against me, and art enemy unto me with the strength of thine hand.
30.22: Thou takest me up and causest me to ride upon the wind, and makest my strength to fail.
30.23: Surely I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all the living.
30.24: Doubtless none can stretch his hand unto the grave, though they cry in his destruction.
30.25: Did not I weep with him that was in trouble? was not my soul in heaviness for the poor?
30.26: Yet when I looked for good, evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
30.27: My bowels did boil without rest: for the days of affliction are come upon me.
30.28: I went mourning without sun: I stood up in the Congregation and cried.
30.29: I am a brother to the Dragons, and a companion to the Ostriches.
30.30: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burnt with heat.
30.31: Therefore mine harp is turned to mourning, and mine organs into the voice of them that weep.

31.1: I made a covenant with mine eyes: why then should I think on a maid?
31.2: For what portion should I have of God from above? and what inheritance of the almighty from on high?
31.3: Is not destruction to the wicked, and strange punishment to the workers of iniquity?
31.4: Doth not he behold my ways, and tell all my steps?
31.5: If I have walked in vanity, or if my foot hath made haste to deceit?
31.6: Let God weigh me in the just balance, and he shall know my uprightness.
31.7: If my step hath turned out of the way, or mine heart hath walked after mine eye, or if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands,
31.8: Let me sow, and let another eat: yea, let my plants be rooted out.
31.9: If mine heart hath been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid wait at the door of my neighbor,
31.10: Let my wife grind unto another man, and let other men bow down upon her.
31.11: For this is a wickedness, and iniquity to be condemned.
31.12: Yea, this is a fire that shall devour to destruction, and which shall root out all my increase.
31.13: If I did contemn the judgment of my servant, and of my maid, when they did contend with me,
31.14: What then shall I do when God standeth up? and when he shall visit me, what shall I answer?
31.15: He that hath made me in the womb, hath he not made him? hath not he alone fashioned us in the womb?
31.16: If I restrained the poor of their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
31.17: Or have eaten my morsels alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof,
31.18: (For from my youth hath he grown up with me as with a father, and from my mother’s womb have I been a guide unto her.)
31.19: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering,
31.20: If his loins have not blessed me, because he was warmed with the fleece of my sheep,
31.21: If I have lifted up mine hand against the fatherless, when I saw that I might help him in the gate,
31.22: Let mine arm fall from my shoulder, and mine arm be broken from the bone.
31.23: For God’s punishment was fearful unto me, and I could not be delivered from his Highness.
31.24: If I made gold mine hope, or have said to the wedge of gold, Thou art my confidence,
31.25: If I rejoiced because my substance was great, or because mine hand had gotten much,
31.26: If I did behold the sun, when it shined, or the moon walking in her brightness,
31.27: If mine heart did flatter me in secret, or if my mouth did kiss mine hand,
31.28: (This also had been an iniquity to be condemned: for I had denied the God above.)
31.29: If I rejoiced at his destruction that hated me, or was moved to joy when evil came upon him,
31.30: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin, by wishing a curse unto his soul.
31.31: Did not the men of my Tabernacle say, Who shall give us of his flesh? we cannot be satisfied.
31.32: The stranger did not lodge in the street, but I opened my doors unto him, that went by the way.
31.33: If I have hid my sins, as Adam, concealing mine iniquity in my bosom,
31.34: Though I could have made afraid a great multitude, yet the most contemptible of the families did fear me: so I kept silence, and went not out of the door.
31.35: Oh that I had some to hear me! behold my sign that the Almighty will witness for me: though mine adversary should write a book against me,
31.36: Would not I take it upon my shoulder, and bind it as a crown unto me?
31.37: I will tell him the number of my goings, and go unto him as to a prince.
31.38: If my land cry against me, or the furrows thereof complain together,
31.39: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without silver: or if I have grieved the souls of the masters thereof,
31.40:
Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle in the stead of barley.
THE WORDS OF JOB ARE ENDED.

32.1: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he esteemed himself just.
32.2: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled: his wrath, I say, was kindled against Job, because he justified himself more than God.
32.3: Also his anger was kindled against his three friends, because they could not find an answer, and yet condemned Job.
32.4: (Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken: for they were more ancient in years than he.)
32.5: So when Elihu saw, that there was none answer in the mouth of the three men, his wrath was kindled.
32.6: Therefore Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite answered and said, I am young in years, and ye are ancient: therefore I doubted, and was afraid to show you mine opinion.
32.7: For I said, The days shall speak, and the multitude of years shall teach wisdom.
32.8: Surely there is a spirit in man, but the inspiration of the Almighty giveth understanding.
32.9: Great men are not always wise, neither do the aged always understand judgment.
32.10: Therefore I say, Hear me and I will show also mine opinion.
32.11: Behold, I did wait upon your words, and hearkened unto your knowledge, while you sought out reasons.
32.12: Yea, when I had considered you, lo, there was none of you that reproved Job, nor answered his words:
32.13: Lest ye should say, We have found wisdom: for God hath cast him down, and no man.
32.14: Yet hath he not directed his words to me, neither will I answer him by your words.
32.15: Then they fearing, answered no more, but left off their talk.
32.16: When I had waited (for they spake not, but stood still and answered no more)
32.17: Then answered I in my turn, and I showed mine opinion.
32.18: For I am full of matter, and the spirit within me compelleth me.
32.19: Behold, my belly is as the wine, which hath no vent, and like the new bottles that burst.
32.20: Therefore will I speak, that I may take breath: I will open my lips, and will answer.
32.21: I will not now accept the person of man, neither will I give titles to man.
32.22: For I may not give titles, lest my Maker should take me away suddenly.

33.1: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my talk, and hearken unto all my words.
33.2: Behold now, I have opened my mouth: my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.
33.3: My words are in the uprightness of mine heart, and my lips shall speak pure knowledge.
33.4: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
33.5: If thou canst give me answer, prepare thyself and stand before me.
33.6: Behold, I am according to thy wish in God’s stead: I am also formed of the clay.
33.7: Behold, my terror shall not fear thee, neither shall mine hand be heavy upon thee.
33.8: Doubtless thou hast spoken in mine ears, and I have heard the voice of thy words.
33.9: I am clean, without sin: I am innocent and there is none iniquity in me.
33.10: Lo, he hath found occasions against me, and counted me for his enemy.
33.11: He hath put my feet in the stocks, and looketh narrowly unto all my paths.
33.12: Behold, in this hast thou not done right: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
33.13: Why dost thou strive against him? for he doth not give account of all his matters.
33.14: For God speaketh once or twice, and one seeth it not.
33.15: In dreams and visions of the night, when sleep falleth upon men, and they sleep upon their beds,
33.16: Then he openeth the ears of men, even by their corrections, which he had sealed,
33.17: That he might cause man to turn away from his enterprise, and that he might hide the pride of man,
33.18: And keep back his soul from the pit, and that his life should not pass by the sword.
33.19: He is also stricken with sorrow upon his bed, and the grief of his bones is sore,
33.20: So that his life causeth him to abhor bread, and his soul dainty meat.
33.21: His flesh faileth that it cannot be seen, and his bones which were not seen, clatter.
33.22: So his soul draweth to the grave, and his life to the buriers.
33.23: If there be a messenger with him, or an interpreter, one of a thousand to declare unto man his righteousness,
33.24: Then will he have mercy upon him, and will say, Deliver him, that he go not down into the pit: for I have received a reconciliation.
33.25: Then shall his flesh be as fresh as a child’s, and shall return as in the days of his youth.
33.26: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favorable unto him, and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.
33.27: He looketh upon men, and if one say, I have sinned, and perverted righteousness, and it did not profit me,
33.28: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.
33.29: Lo, all these things will God work twice or thrice with a man,
33.30: That he may turn back his soul from the pit, to be illuminated in the light of the living.
33.31: Mark well, O Job, and hear me: keep silence and I will speak.
33.32: If there be matter, answer me, and speak: for I desire to justify thee.
33.33: If thou hast not, hear me: hold thy tongue, and I will teach thee wisdom.

34.2: Hear my words, ye wise men, and hearken unto me ye that have knowledge.
34.3: For the ear trieth the words, as the mouth tasteth meat.
34.4: Let us seek judgment among us, and let us know among ourselves what is good.
34.5: For Job hath said, I am righteous, and God hath taken away my judgment.
34.6: Should I lie in my right? my wound of the arrow is grievous without my sin.
34.7: What man is like Job, that drinketh scornfulness like water?
34.8: Which goeth in the company of them that work iniquity, and walketh with wicked men?
34.9: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should walk with God.
34.10: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of wisdom, God forbid that wickedness should be in God, and iniquity in the Almighty.
34.11: For he will render unto man according to his work, and cause everyone to find according to his way.
34.12: And certainly God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
34.13: Whom hath he appointed over the earth besides himself? or who hath placed the whole world?
34.14: If he set his heart upon man, and gather unto himself his spirit and his breath,
34.15: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall return unto dust.
34.16: And if thou hast understanding, hear this, and hearken to the voice of my words.
34.17: Shall he that hateth judgment, govern? and wilt thou judge him wicked that is most just?
34.18: Wilt thou say unto a king, Thou art wicked? or to princes, Ye are ungodly?
34.19: How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, and regardeth not the rich, more than the poor? for they be all the work of his hands.
34.20: They shall die suddenly, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and they shall pass forth and take away the mighty without hand.
34.21: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.
34.22: There is no darkness nor shadow of death, that the workers of iniquity might be hid therein.
34.23: For he will not lay on man so much, that he should enter into judgment with God.
34.24: He shall break the mighty without seeking, and shall set up others in their stead.
34.25: Therefore shall he declare their works: he shall turn the night, and they shall be destroyed.
34.26: He striketh them as wicked men in the places of the seers,
34.27: Because they have turned back from him, and would not consider all his ways:
34.28: So that they have caused the voice of the poor to come unto him, and he hath heard the cry of the afflicted.
34.29: And when he giveth quietness, who can make trouble? and when he hideth his face, who can behold him, whether it be upon nations, or upon a man only?
34.30: Because the hypocrite doth reign, and because the people are snared.
34.31: Surely it appertaineth unto God to say, I have pardoned, I will not destroy.
34.32: But if I see not, teach thou me: if I have done wickedly, I will do no more.
34.33: Will he perform the thing through thee? for thou hast reproved it, because that thou hast chosen, and not I: now speak what thou knowest.
34.34: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.
34.35: Job hath not spoken of knowledge, neither were his words according to wisdom.
34.36: I desire that Job may be tried, unto the end, touching the answers for wicked men.
34.37: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

35.2: Thinkest thou this right, that thou hast said, I am more righteous than God?
35.3: For thou hast said, What profiteth it thee, and what availeth it me, to purge me from my sin?
35.4: Therefore will I answer thee, and thy companions with thee.
35.5: Look unto the heaven, and see and behold the clouds which are higher than thou.
35.6: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him, yea, when thy sins be many, what doest thou unto him?
35.7: If thou be righteous, what givest thou unto him? or what receiveth he at thine hand?
35.8: Thy wickedness may hurt a man as thou art: and thy righteousness may profit the son of man.
35.9: They cause many that are oppressed, to cry, which cry out for the violence of the mighty.
35.10: But none saith, Where is God that made me, which giveth songs in the night?
35.11: Which teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and giveth us more wisdom than the fowls of the heaven.
35.12: Then they cry because of the violence of the wicked, but he answereth not.
35.13: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
35.14: Although thou sayest to God, Thou wilt not regard it, yet judgment is before him: trust thou in him.
35.15: But now because his anger hath not visited, nor called to count the evil with great extremity,
35.16: Therefore Job openeth his mouth in vain, and multiplieth words without knowledge.

36.2: Suffer me a little and I will instruct thee: for I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.
36.3: I will fetch my knowledge afar off, and will attribute righteousness unto my maker.
36.4: For truly my words shall not be false, and he that is perfect in knowledge, speaketh with thee.
36.5: Behold, the mighty God casteth away none that is mighty and valiant of courage.
36.6: He maintaineth not the wicked, but he giveth judgment to the afflicted.
36.7: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous, but they are with kings in the throne, where he placeth them forever: thus they are exalted.
36.8: And if they be bound in fetters and tied with the cords of affliction,
36.9: Then will he show them their work and their sins, because they have been proud.
36.10: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth them that they return from iniquity.
36.11: If they obey and serve him, they shall end their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures:
36.12: But if they will not obey, they shall pass by the sword and perish without knowledge.
36.13: But the hypocrites of heart increase the wrath: for they call not when he bindeth them.
36.14: Their soul dieth in youth, and their life among the whoremongers.
36.15: He delivereth the poor in his afflictions, and openeth their ear in trouble.
36.16: Even so would he have taken thee out of the straight place into a broad place, and not shut up beneath: and that which resteth upon thy table had been full of fat.
36.17: But thou art full of the judgment of the wicked, though judgment and equity maintain all things.
36.18: For God’s wrath is, lest he should take thee away in thine abundance: for no multitude of gifts can deliver thee.
36.19: Will he regard thy riches? he regardeth not gold, nor all them that excel in strength.
36.20: Be not careful in the night, how he destroyeth the people out of their place.
36.21: Take thou heed: look not to iniquity: for thou hast chosen it rather than affliction.
36.22: Behold, God exalteth by his power: what teacher is like him?
36.23: Who hath appointed to him his way? or who can say, Thou hast done wickedly?
36.24: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
36.25: All men see it, and men behold it afar off.
36.26: Behold, God is excellent, and we know him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
36.27: When he restraineth the drops of water, the rain poureth down by the vapor thereof,
36.28: Which rain the clouds do drop and let fall abundantly upon man.
36.29: Who can know the divisions of the clouds, and the thunders of his Tabernacle?
36.30: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.
36.31: For thereby he judgeth the people, and giveth meat abundantly.
36.32: He covereth the light with the clouds, and commanded them to go against it.
36.33: His companion showeth him therefore, and there is anger in rising up.

37.1: At this also mine heart is astonied, and is moved out of his place.
37.2: Hear the sound of his voice, and the noise that goeth out of his mouth.
37.3: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his light unto the ends of the world.
37.4: After it a noise soundeth: he thundereth with the voice of his majesty, and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.
37.5: God thundereth marvelously with his voice: he worketh great things, which we know not.
37.6: For he saith to the snow, Be thou upon the earth likewise to the small rain and to the great rain of his power.
37.7: With the force thereof he shutteth up every man, that all men may know his work.
37.8: Then the beasts go into the den, and remain in their places.
37.9: The whirlwind cometh out of the South, and the cold from the North wind.
37.10: At the breath of God the frost is given, and the breadth of the waters is made narrow.
37.11: He maketh also the clouds to labor, to water the earth, and scattereth the cloud of his light.
37.12: And it is turned about by his government, that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the whole world:
37.13: Whether it be for punishment, or for his land, or of mercy, he causeth it to come.
37.14: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand and consider the wondrous works of God.
37.15: Didst thou know when God disposed them? and caused the light of his cloud to shine?
37.16: Hast thou known the variety of the cloud, and the wondrous works of him that is perfect in knowledge?
37.17: Or how thy clothes are warm, when he maketh the earth quiet through the South wind?
37.18: Hast thou stretched out the heavens, which are strong, and as a molten glass?
37.19: Tell us what we shall say unto him: for we cannot dispose our matter because of darkness.
37.20: Shall it be told him when I speak? or shall man speak when he shall be destroyed?
37.21: And now men see not the light, which shineth in the clouds, but the wind passeth and cleanseth them.
37.22: The brightness cometh out of the North: the praise thereof is to God, which is terrible.
37.23: It is the Almighty: we cannot find him out: he is excellent in power and judgment, and abundant in justice: he afflicteth not.
37.24: Let men therefore fear him: for he will not regard any that are wise in their own conceit.

38.1: Then answered the Lord unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
38.2: Who is this that darkeneth the counsel by words without knowledge?
38.3: Gird up now thy loins like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
38.4: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
38.5: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest, or who hath stretched the line over it:
38.6: Whereupon are the foundations thereof set: or who laid the cornerstone thereof:
38.7: When the stars of the morning praised me together, and all the children of God rejoiced:
38.8: Or who hath shut up the Sea with doors, when it issued and came forth as out of the womb:
38.9: When I made the clouds as a covering thereof, and darkness as the swaddling bands thereof:
38.10: When I establisheth my commandment upon it, and set bars and doors,
38.11: And said, hitherto shalt thou come, but no further, and here shall it stay thy proud waves.
38.12: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days? hast thou caused the morning to know his place?
38.13: That it might take hold of the corners of the earth, and that the wicked might be shaken out of it?
38.14: It is turned as clay to fashion, and all stand up as a garment.
38.15: And from the wicked their light shall be taken away, and the high arm shall be broken.
38.16: Hast thou entered into the bottoms of the sea? or hast thou walked to seek out the depth?
38.17: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the gates of the shadow of death?
38.18: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? tell if thou knowest all this.
38.19: Where is the way where light dwelleth? and where is the place of darkness,
38.20: That thou shouldest receive it in the bounds thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths to the house thereof?
38.21: Knewest thou it, because thou wast then born? and because the number of thy days is great?
38.22: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,
38.23: Which I have hid against the time of trouble, against the day of war and battle?
38.24: By what way is the light parted, which scattereth the East wind upon the earth?
38.25: Who hath divided the spouts for the rain? or the way for the lightning of the thunders,
38.26: To cause it to rain on the earth where no man is, and in the wilderness where there is no man?
38.27: To fulfill the wild and waste place, and to cause the bud of the herb to spring forth?
38.28: Who is the father of the rain? or who hath begotten the drops of the dew?
38.29: Out of whose womb came the ice? who hath engendered the frost of the heaven?
38.30: The waters are hid as with a stone: and the face of the depth is frozen.
38.31: Canst thou restrain the sweet influences of the Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?
38.32: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in their time? canst thou also guide Arcturus with his sons?
38.33: Knowest thou the course of heaven, or canst thou set the rule thereof in the earth?
38.34: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that the abundance of water may cover thee?
38.35: Canst thou send the lightnings that they may walk, and say unto thee, Lo, here we are?
38.36: Who hath put wisdom in the reins? or who hath given the heart understanding?
38.37: Who can number clouds by wisdom? or who can cause to cease the bottles of heaven,
38.38: When the earth groweth into hardness, and the clots are fast together?

39.1: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the lion’s whelps,
39.2: When they crouch in their places, and remain in the covert to lie in wait?
39.3: Who prepareth for the raven his meat, when his birds cry unto God, wandering for lack of meat?
39.4: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats bring forth young? or dost thou mark when the hinds do calve?
39.5: Canst thou number the months that they fulfill? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
39.6: They bow themselves: they bruise their young and cast out their sorrows.
39.7: Yet their young wax fat, and grow up with corn: they go forth and return not unto them.
39.8: Who hath set the wild ass at liberty? or who hath loosed the bonds of the wild ass?
39.9: It is I which have made the wilderness his house, and the salt places his dwellings.
39.10: He derideth the multitude of the city: he heareth not the cry of the driver.
39.11: He seeketh out the mountain for his pasture, and searcheth after every green thing.
39.12: Will the unicorn serve thee? or will he tarry by thy crib?
39.13: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band to labor in the furrow? or will he plow the valleys after thee?
39.14: Wilt thou trust in him, because his strength is great, and cast off thy labor unto him?
39.15: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it unto thy barn?
39.16: Hast thou given the pleasant wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?
39.17: Which leaveth his eggs in the earth, and maketh them hot in the dust,
39.18: And forgetteth that the foot might scatter them, or that the wild beast might break them.
39.19: He showeth himself cruel unto his young ones, as they were not his, and is without fear, as if he travailed in vain.
39.20: For God had deprived him of wisdom, and hath given him no part of understanding.
39.21: When time is, he mounteth on high: he mocketh the horse and his rider.
39.22: Hast thou given the horse strength, or covered his neck with neighing?
39.23: Hast thou made him afraid as the grasshopper? his strong neighing is fearful.
39.24: He diggeth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth forth to meet the harnessed man.
39.25: He mocketh at fear, and is not afraid, and turneth not back from the sword,
39.26: Though the quiver rattle against him, the glittering spear and the shield.
39.27: He swalloweth the ground for fierceness and rage, and he believeth not that it is the noise of the trumpet.
39.28: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha: he smelleth the battle afar off, and the noise of the captains, and the shouting.
39.29: Shall the hawk fly by thy wisdom, stretching out his wings even toward the South?
39.30: Doth the eagle mount up at thy commandment, or make his nest on high?
39.31: She abideth and remaineth in the rock, even upon the top of the rock, and the tower,
39.32: From thence she spieth for meat, and her eyes behold afar off.
39.33: His young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.
39.34: Moreover the Lord spake unto Job, and said,
39.35: Is this to learn, to strive with the Almighty? he that reproveth God, let him answer to it.
39.36: Then Job answered the Lord, saying,
39.37: Behold, I am vile: what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.
39.38: Once have I spoken, but I will answer no more, yea twice, but I will proceed no further.

40.1: Again the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
40.2: Gird up now thy loins like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
40.3: Wilt thou disannul my judgment? or wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be justified?
40.4: Or hast thou an arm like God? or dost thou thunder with a voice like him?
40.5: Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency, and array thyself with beauty and glory.
40.6: Cast abroad the indignation of thy wrath, and behold everyone that is proud, and abase him.
40.7: Look on everyone that is arrogant, and bring him low: and destroy the wicked in their place.
40.8: Hide them in the dust together, and bind their faces in a secret place.
40.9: Then will I confess unto thee also, that thy right hand can save thee.
40.10: Behold now Behemoth (whom I made with thee) which eateth grass as an ox.
40.11: Behold now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.
40.12: When he taketh pleasure, his tail is like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.
40.13: His bones are like staves of brass, and his small bones like staves of iron.
40.14: He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him, will make his sword to approach unto him.
40.15: Surely the mountains bring him forth grass, where all the beasts of the field play.
40.16: Lieth he under the trees in the covert of the reed and fens?
40.17: Can the trees cover him with their shadow? or can the willows of the river compass him about?
40.18: Behold, he spoileth the river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.
40.19: He taketh it with his eyes, and thrusteth his nose through whatsoever meeteth him.
40.20: Canst thou draw out Leviathan with an hook, and with a line which thou shalt cast down unto his tongue?
40.21: Canst thou cast an hook into his nose? canst thou pierce his jaws with an angle?
40.22: Will he make many prayers unto thee? and speak thee fair?
40.23: Will he make a covenant with thee? and wilt thou take him as a servant forever?
40.24: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maids?
40.25: Shall the companions banquet with him? shall they divide him among the merchants?
40.26: Canst thou fill the basket with his skin? or the fishpanier with his head?
40.27: Lay thine hand upon him: remember the battle, and do no more so.
40.28: Behold, his hope is in vain: for shall not one perish even at the sight of him?

41.1: None is so fierce that dare stir him up. Who is he then that can stand before me?
41.2: Who hath prevented me that I should make an end? All under heaven is mine.
41.3: I will not keep silence concerning his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
41.4: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who shall come to him with a double bridle?
41.5: Who shall open the doors of his face? his teeth are fearful round about.
41.6: The majesty of his scales is like strong shields, and are sure sealed.
41.7: One is set to another, that no wind can come between them.
41.8: One is joined to another: they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.
41.9: His sneezings make the light to shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
41.10: Out of his mouth go lamps, and sparks of fire leap out.
41.11: Out of his nostrils cometh out smoke, as out of a boiling pot or caldron.
41.12: His breath maketh the coals burn: for a flame goeth out of his mouth.
41.13: In his neck remaineth strength, and labor is rejected before his face.
41.14: The members of his body are joined: they are strong in themselves, and cannot be moved.
41.15: His heart is as strong as a stone, and as hard as the nether millstone.
41.16: The mighty are afraid of his majesty, and for fear they faint in themselves.
41.17: When the sword doth touch him, he will not rise up, nor for the spear, dart nor habergeon.
41.18: He esteemeth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
41.19: The archer cannot make him flee: the stones of the sling are turneth into stubble unto him.
41.20: The darts are counted as straw: and he laugheth at the shaking of the spear.
41.21: Sharp stones are under him, and he spreadeth sharp things upon the mire.
41.22: He maketh the depth to boil like a pot, and maketh the Sea like a pot of ointment.
41.23: He maketh a path to shine after him, one would think the depth as an hoar head.
41.24: In the earth there is none like him: he is made without fear.
41.25: He beholdeth all high things: he is a King over all the children of pride.

42.1: Then Job answered the Lord, and said,
42.2: I know that thou canst do all things, and that there is no thought hid from thee.
42.3: Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I spoken that I understood not, even things too wonderful for me, and which I knew not.
42.4: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
42.5: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear, but now mine eye seeth thee.
42.6: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.
42.7: Now after that the Lord had spoken these words unto Job, the Lord also said unto Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, like my servant Job.
42.8: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks, and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering, and my servant Job shall pray for you: for I will accept him, lest I should put you to shame, because ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.
42.9: So Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, went, and did according as the Lord had said unto them, and the Lord accepted Job.
42.10: Then the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice so much as he had before.
42.11: Then came unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house, and had compassion on him, and comforted him for all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him, and every man gave him a piece of money, and everyone an earring of gold.
42.12: So the Lord blessed the last days of Job more than the first: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
42.13: He had also seven sons, and three daughters.
42.14: And he called the name of one Jemimah, and the name of the second Keziah, and the name of the third Keren-Happuch.
42.15: In all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job, and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
42.16: And after this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his son’s sons, even four generations.
42.17: So Job died, being old, and full of days.

1.1: Blessed is the man that doth not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of the scornful.
1.2: But his delight is in the law of the Lord, and in his law doth he meditate day and night.
1.3: For he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of waters, that will bring forth her fruits in due season: whose leaf shall not fade: so whatsoever he shall do, shall prosper.
1.4: The wicked are not so, but as the chaff, which the wind driveth away.
1.5: Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
1.6: For the Lord knoweth the way of the righteous, and the way of the wicked shall perish.

2.1: Why do the heathen rage, and the people murmur in vain.
2.2: The kings of the earth band themselves, and the Princes are assembled together against the Lord, and against his Christ.
2.3: Let us break their bands, and cast their cords from us.
2.4: But he that dwelleth in the heaven shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.
2.5: Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure, saying,
2.6: Even I have set my King upon Zion mine holy mountain.
2.7: I will declare the decree: that is, the Lord hath said unto me, Thou art my son; this day have I begotten thee.
2.8: Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the ends of the earth for thy possession.
2.9: Thou shalt crush them with a scepter of iron, and break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.
2.10: Be wise now therefore, ye kings: be learned ye judges of the earth.
2.11: Serve the Lord in fear, and rejoice in trembling.
2.12: Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish in the way, when his wrath shall suddenly burn. Blessed are all that trust in him.

3.1: Lord, how are mine adversaries increased? how many rise against me?
3.2: Many say to my soul, There is no help for him in God. Selah.
3.3: But thou Lord art a buckler for me, my glory, and the lifter up of mine head.
3.4: I did call unto the Lord with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy mountain. Selah.
3.5: I laid me down and slept, and rose up again: for the Lord sustained me.
3.6: I will not be afraid for ten thousand of the people, that should beset me round about.
3.7: O Lord, arise: help me, my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies upon the cheekbone: thou hast broken the teeth of the wicked.
3.8: Salvation belongeth unto the Lord, and thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.

4.1: Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast set me at liberty, when I was in distress: have mercy upon me, and hearken unto my prayer.
4.2: O ye sons of men, how long will ye turn my glory into shame, loving vanity, and seeking lies? Selah.
4.3: For be ye sure that the Lord hath chosen to himself a godly man, the Lord will hear when I call unto him.
4.4: Tremble and sin not: examine your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.
4.5: Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in the Lord.
4.6: Many say, Who will show us any good? but Lord, lift up the light of thy countenance upon us.
4.7: Thou hast given me more joy of heart, than they have had, when their wheat and their wine did abound.
4.8: I will lay me down, and also sleep in peace: for thou, Lord, only makest me dwell in safety.

5.1: Hear my words, O Lord: understand my meditation.
5.2: Hearken unto the voice of my cry, my king and my God: for unto thee do I pray.
5.3: Hear my voice in the morning, O Lord: for in the morning will I direct me unto thee, and I will wait.
5.4: For thou art not a God that loveth wickedness, neither shall evil dwell with thee.
5.5: The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: for thou hatest all them that work iniquity.
5.6: Thou shalt destroy them that speak lies: the Lord will abhor the bloody man and deceitful.
5.7: But I will come into thine house in the multitude of thy mercy: and in thy fear will I worship toward thine holy Temple.
5.8: Lead me, O Lord, in thy righteousness, because of mine enemies: make thy way plain before my face.
5.9: For no constancy is in their mouth: within they are very corruption: their throat is an open sepulcher, and they flatter with their tongue.
5.10: Destroy them, O God, let them fall from their counsels: cast them out for the multitude of their iniquities, because they have rebelled against thee.
5.11: And let all them that trust in thee, rejoice and triumph forever, and cover thou them: and let them that love thy name, rejoice in thee.
5.12: For thou Lord, wilt bless the righteous, and with favor wilt compass him, as with a shield.

6.1: O Lord, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chastise me in thy wrath.
6.2: Have mercy upon me, O Lord, for I am weak: O Lord heal me, for my bones are vexed.
6.3: My soul is also sore troubled: but Lord, how long wilt thou delay?
6.4: Return, O Lord: deliver my soul: save me for thy mercy’s sake.
6.5: For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall praise thee?
6.6: I fainted in my mourning: I cause my bed every night to swim, and water my couch with my tears.
6.7: Mine eye is dimmed for despite, and sunk in because of all mine enemies.
6.8: Away from me all ye workers of iniquity: for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.
6.9: The Lord hath heard my petition: the Lord will receive my prayer.
6.10: All mine enemies shall be confounded and sore vexed: they shall be turned back, and put to shame suddenly.

7.1: O Lord my God, in thee I put my trust: save me from all that persecute me, and deliver me,
7.2: Lest he devour my soul like a lion, and tear it in pieces, while there is none to help.
7.3: O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, if there be any wickedness in mine hands,
7.4: If I have rewarded evil unto him that had peace with me, (yea I have delivered him that vexed me without cause.)
7.5: Then let the enemies persecute my soul, and take it: yea, let him tread my life down upon the earth, and lay mine honor in the dust. Selah.
7.6: Arise, O Lord, in thy wrath, and lift up thyself against the rage of mine enemies, and awake for me according to the judgment that thou hast appointed.
7.7: So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about: for their sakes therefore return on high.
7.8: The Lord shall judge the people: judge thou me, O Lord, according to my righteousness, and according to mine innocency that is in me.
7.9: Oh let the malice of the wicked come to an end: but guide thou the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.
7.10: My defense is in God, who preserveth the upright in heart.
7.11: God judgeth the righteous, and him that contemneth God, every day.
7.12: Except he turn, he hath whet his sword: he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.
7.13: He hath also prepared him deadly weapons: he will ordain his arrows for them that persecute me.
7.14: Behold, he shall travail with wickedness: for he hath conceived mischief, but he shall bring forth a lie.
7.15: He hath made a pit, and dug it, and is fallen into the pit that he made.
7.16: His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his cruelty shall fall upon his own pate.
7.17: I will praise the Lord according to his righteousness, and will sing praise to the Name of the Lord most high.

8.1: O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy Name in all the world! which hast set thy glory above the heavens.
8.2: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength, because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger.
8.3: When I behold thine heavens, even the works of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained,
8.4: What is man, say I, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man that thou visitest him?
8.5: For thou hast made him a little lower than God, and crowned him with glory and worship.
8.6: Thou hast made him to have dominion in the works of thine hands, thou hast put all things under his feet:
8.7: All sheep and oxen: yea, and the beasts of the field:
8.8: The fowls of the air, and the fish of the sea, and that which passeth through the paths of the seas.
8.9: O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy Name in all the world!

9.1: I will praise the Lord with my whole heart: I will speak of all thy marvelous works.
9.2: I will be glad, and rejoice in thee: I will sing praise to thy Name, O most High.
9.3: For that mine enemies are turned back: they shall fall and perish at thy presence.
9.4: For thou hast maintained my right and my cause: thou art set in the throne, and judgest right.
9.5: Thou hast rebuked the heathen: thou hast destroyed the wicked: thou hast put out their name forever and ever.
9.6: O enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end, and thou hast destroyed the cities: their memorial is perished with them.
9.7: But the Lord shall sit forever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment.
9.8: For he shall judge the world in righteousness, and shall judge the people with equity.
9.9: The Lord also will be a refuge for the poor, a refuge in due time, even in affliction.
9.10: And they that know thy Name, will trust in thee: for thou, Lord, hast not failed them that seek thee.
9.11: Sing praises to the Lord, which dwelleth in Zion: show the people his works.
9.12: For when he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth it, and forgetteth not the complaint of the poor.
9.13: Have mercy upon me, O Lord: consider my trouble which I suffer of them that hate me, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death,
9.14: That I may show all thy praises within the gates of the daughter of Zion, and rejoice in thy salvation.
9.15: The heathen are sunken down in the pit that they made: in the net that they hid, is their foot taken.
9.16: The Lord is known by executing judgment: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands, Higgaion. Selah.
9.17: The wicked shall turn into hell, and all nations that forget God.
9.18: For the poor shall not be always forgotten: the hope of the afflicted shall not perish forever.
9.19: Up Lord: let not man prevail: let the heathen be judged in thy sight.
9.20: Put them in fear, O Lord, that the heathen may know that they are but men. Selah.

10.1: Why standest thou far off, O Lord, and hidest thee in due time, even in affliction?
10.2: The wicked with pride doth persecute the poor; let them be taken in the crafts that they have imagined.
10.3: For the wicked hath made boast of his own heart’s desire, and the covetous blesseth himself, he contemneth the Lord.
10.4: The wicked is so proud, that he seeketh not for God: he thinketh always, There is no God.
10.5: His ways always prosper: thy judgments are high above his sight; therefore defieth he all his enemies.
10.6: He saith in his heart, I shall never be moved, nor be in danger.
10.7: His mouth is full of cursing, and deceit, and fraud; under his tongue is mischief and iniquity.
10.8: He lieth in wait in the villages; in the secret places doth he murder the innocent; his eyes are bent against the poor.
10.9: He lieth in wait secretly, even as a lion in his den; he lieth in wait to spoil the poor; he doth spoil the poor, when he draweth him into his net.
10.10: He croucheth and boweth; therefore heaps of the poor do fall by his might.
10.11: He hath said in his heart, God hath forgotten, he hideth away his face, and will never see.
10.12: Arise, O Lord God, lift up thine hand; forget not the poor.
10.13: Wherefore doth the wicked contemn God? he saith in his heart, Thou wilt not regard.
10.14: Yet thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and wrong; that thou mayest take it into thine hands; the poor committeth himself unto thee; for thou art the helper of the fatherless.
10.15: Break thou the arm of the wicked and malicious; search his wickedness, and thou shalt find none.
10.16: The Lord is King forever and ever; the heathen are destroyed forth of his land.
10.17: Lord, thou hast heard the desire of the poor; thou preparest their heart; thou bendest thine ear to them,
10.18: To judge the fatherless and poor, that earthly man cause to fear no more.

11.1: In the Lord put I my trust; how say ye then to my soul, Flee to your mountain as a bird?
11.2: For lo, the wicked bend their bow, and make ready their arrows upon the string, that they may secretly shoot at them which are upright in heart.
11.3: For the foundations are cast down, what hath the righteous done?
11.4: The Lord is in his holy palace; the Lord’s throne is in the heaven; his eyes will consider; his eyelids will try the children of men.
11.5: The Lord will try the righteous; but the wicked, and him that loveth iniquity, doth his soul hate.
11.6: Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire, and brimstone, and stormy tempest; this is the portion of their cup.
11.7: For the righteous Lord loveth righteousness: his countenance doth behold the just.

12.1: Help Lord, for there is not a godly man left: for the faithful are failed from among the children of men.
12.2: They speak deceitfully every one with his neighbor, flattering with their lips, and speak with a double heart.
12.3: The Lord cut off all flattering lips, and the tongue that speaketh proud things:
12.4: Which have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own; who is Lord over us?
12.5: Now for the oppression of the needy, and for the sighs of the poor, I will up, saith the Lord, and will set at liberty him, whom the wicked hath [snared].
12.6: The words of the Lord are pure words, as the silver, tried in a furnace of earth, fined sevenfold.
12.7: Thou wilt keep them, O Lord; thou wilt preserve him from this generation forever.
12.8: The wicked walk on every side; when they are exalted, it is a shame for the sons of men.

13.1: How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord, forever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
13.2: How long shall I take counsel within myself having weariness daily in mine heart? how long shall mine enemy be exalted above me?
13.3: Behold, and hear me, O Lord my God: lighten mine eyes, that I sleep not in death.
13.4: Lest mine enemy say, I have prevailed against him: and they that afflict me, rejoice, when I slide.
13.5: But I trust in thy mercy: mine heart shall rejoice in thy salvation; I will sing to the Lord, because he hath dealt lovingly with me.

14.1: The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God: they have corrupted, and done an abominable work: there is none that doeth good.
14.2: The Lord looked down from heaven upon the children of men, to see if there were any that would understand, and seek God.
14.3: All are gone out of the way: they are all corrupt: there is none that doeth good, no not one.
14.4: Do not all the workers of iniquity know that they eat up my people, as they eat bread? they call not upon the Lord.
14.5: There they shall be taken with fear, because God is in the generation of the just.
14.6: You have made a mock at the counsel of the poor, because the Lord is his trust.
14.7:
Oh give salvation unto Israel out of Zion: when the Lord turneth the captivity of his people, then Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
Note that of Psalm 14:5-7, which are put into the common translation, and may seem unto some to be left out in this, are not in the same Psalm in the Hebrew text, but rather are put in more fully to express the manners of the wicked, and are gathered out of Psalms 5, 10, 36, 140; Isa. 59, and are alleged by S. Paul, and placed together in Romans 3.

15.1: Lord, who shall dwell in thy Tabernacle? who shall rest in thine holy Mountain?
15.2: He that walketh uprightly and worketh righteousness, and speaketh the truth in his heart.
15.3: He that slandereth not with his tongue, nor doeth evil to his neighbor, nor receiveth a false report against his neighbor.
15.4: In whose eyes a vile person is contemned, but he honoreth them that fear the Lord: he that sweareth to his own hindrance and changeth not.
15.5: He that giveth not his money unto usury, nor taketh reward against the innocent: he that doeth these things, shall never be moved.

16.1: Preserve me, O GOD: for in thee do I trust.
16.2: O my soul, thou hast said unto the Lord, Thou art my Lord: my well doing extendeth not to thee,
16.3: But to the Saints that are in the earth, and to the excellent: all my delight is in them.
16.4: The sorrows of them, that offer to another god, shall be multiplied: their offerings of blood will I not offer, neither make mention of their names with my lips.
16.5: The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou shalt maintain my lot.
16.6: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places: yea, I have a fair heritage.
16.7: I will praise the Lord, who hath given me counsel: my reins also teach me in the nights.
16.8: I have set the Lord always before me: for he is at my right hand: therefore I shall not slide.
16.9: Wherefore mine heart is glad, and my tongue rejoiceth: my flesh also doth rest in hope.
16.10: For thou wilt not leave my soul in the grave: neither wilt thou suffer thine holy One to see corruption.
16.11: Thou wilt show me the path of life: in thy presence is the fullness of joy: and at thy right hand there are pleasures forevermore.

17.1: Hear the right, O Lord, consider my cry: hearken unto my prayer of lips unfeigned.
17.2: Let my sentence come forth from thy presence, and let thine eyes behold equity.
17.3: Thou hast proved and visited mine heart in the night: thou hast tried me, and foundest nothing: for I was purposed that my mouth should not offend.
17.4: Concerning the works of men, by the words of thy lips I kept me from the paths of the cruel man.
17.5: Stay my steps in thy paths, that my feet do not slide.
17.6: I have called upon thee: surely thou wilt hear me, O God: incline thine ear to me, and hearken unto my words.
17.7: Show thy marvelous mercies: thou that art the Savior of them that trust in thee, from such as resist thy right hand.
17.8: Keep me as the apple of the eye: hide me under the shadow of thy wings,
17.9: From the wicked that oppress me, from mine enemies, which compass me round about for my soul.
17.10: They are enclosed in their own fat, and they have spoken proudly with their mouth.
17.11: They have compassed us now in our steps: they have set their eyes to bring down to the ground:
17.12: Like as a lion that is greedy of prey, and as it were a Lion’s whelp lurking in secret places.
17.13: Up Lord, disappoint him: cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked with thy sword,
17.14: From men by thine hand, O Lord, from men of the world, who have their portion in this life, whose bellies thou fillest with thine hid treasure: their children have enough, and leave the rest of their substance for their children.
17.15: But I will behold thy face in righteousness, and when I wake, I shall be satisfied with thine image.

18.1: I will love thee dearly, O Lord my strength.
18.2: The Lord is my rock, and my fortress, and he that delivereth me, my God and my strength: in him will I trust, my shield, the horn also of my salvation, and my refuge.
18.3: I will call upon the Lord, which is worthy to be praised: so shall I be safe from mine enemies.
18.4: The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of wickedness made me afraid.
18.5: The sorrows of the grave have compassed me about: the snares of death overtook me.
18.6: But in my trouble did I call upon the Lord, and cried unto my God: he heard my voice out of his Temple, and my cry did come before him, even into his ears.
18.7: Then the earth trembled and quaked: the foundations also of the mountains moved and shook, because he was angry.
18.8: Smoke went out at his nostrils, and a consuming fire out of his mouth: coals were kindled thereat.
18.9: He bowed the heavens also and came down, and darkness was under his feet.
18.10: And he rode upon Cherub, and did fly, and he came flying upon the wings of the wind.
18.11: He made darkness his secret place, and his pavilion round about him, even darkness of waters, and clouds of the air.
18.12: At the brightness of his presence his clouds passed, hailstones and coals of fire.
18.13: The Lord also thundered in the heaven, and the Highest gave his voice, hailstones and coals of fire.
18.14: Then he sent out his arrows and scattered them, and he increased lightnings and destroyed them.
18.15: And the channels of waters were seen, and the foundations of the world were discovered at thy rebuking, O Lord, at the blasting of the breath of thy nostrils.
18.16: He hath sent down from above and taken me: he hath drawn me out of many waters.
18.17: He hath delivered me from my strong enemy, and from them which hate me: for they were too strong for me.
18.18: They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the Lord was my stay.
18.19: He brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me because he favored me.
18.20: The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the pureness of mine hand he recompensed me:
18.21: Because I kept the ways of the Lord, and did not wickedly against my God.
18.22: For all his laws were before me, and I did not cast away his commandments from me.
18.23: I was upright also with him, and have kept me from my wickedness.
18.24: Therefore the Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness, and according to the pureness of mine hands in his sight.
18.25: With the godly thou wilt show thyself godly: with the upright man thou wilt show thyself upright.
18.26: With the pure thou wilt show thyself pure, and with the froward thou wilt show thyself froward.
18.27: Thus thou wilt save the poor people, and wilt cast down to proud looks.
18.28: Surely thou wilt light my candle: the Lord my God will lighten my darkness.
18.29: For by thee I have broken through an host, and by my God I have leaped over a wall.
18.30: The way of God is uncorrupt: the word of the Lord is tried in the fire: he is a shield to all that trust in him.
18.31: For who is God besides the Lord? and who is mighty save our God?
18.32: God girdeth me with strength, and maketh my way upright.
18.33: He maketh my feet like hind’s feet, and setteth me upon mine high places.
18.34: He teacheth mine hands to fight: so that a bow of brass is broken with mine arms.
18.35: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation, and thy right hand hath stayed me, and thy lovingkindness hath caused me to increase.
18.36: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me, and my heels have not slid.
18.37: I have pursued mine enemies, and taken them, and have not turned again till I had consumed them.
18.38: I have wounded them, that they were not able to rise, they are fallen under my feet.
18.39: For thou hast girded me with strength to battle: them that rose against me, thou hast subdued under me.
18.40: And thou hast given me the necks of mine enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
18.41: They cried, but there was none to save them, even unto the Lord, but he answered them not.
18.42: Then I did beat them small as the dust before the wind: I did tread them flat as the clay in the streets.
18.43: Thou hast delivered me from the contentions of the people: thou hast made me the head of the heathen, a people, whom I have not known, shall serve me.
18.44: As soon as they hear they shall obey me: the strangers shall be in subjection to me.
18.45: Strangers shall shrink away, and fear in their pure chambers.
18.46: Let the Lord live, and blessed be my strength, and the God of my salvation be exalted.
18.47: It is God that giveth me power to avenge me, and subdued the people under me.
18.48: O my deliverer from mine enemies, even thou hast set me up from those that rose against me; thou hast delivered me from the cruel man.
18.49: Therefore I will praise thee, O Lord, among the nations, and will sing unto thy Name.
18.50: Great deliverances giveth he unto his king, and showeth mercy to his anointed, even to David, and to his seed forever.

19.1: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament showeth the work of his hands.
19.2: Day unto day uttereth the same, and night unto night teacheth knowledge.
19.3: There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.
19.4: Their line is gone forth through all the earth, and their words into the ends of the world: in them hath he set a tabernacle for the Sun.
19.5: Which cometh forth as a bridegroom out of his chamber, and rejoiceth like a mighty man to run his race.
19.6: His going out is from the end of the heaven, and his compass is unto the ends of the same, and none is hid from the heat thereof.
19.7: The Law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, and giveth wisdom unto the simple.
19.8: The statutes of the Lord are right, and rejoice the heart, the commandment of the Lord is pure, and giveth light unto the eyes.
19.9: The fear of the Lord is clean, and endureth forever: the judgments of the Lord are truth: they are righteous altogether,
19.10: And more to be desired than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey, and the honeycomb.
19.11: Moreover by them is thy servant made circumspect, and in keeping of them there is great reward.
19.12: Who can understand his faults? cleanse me from secret faults.
19.13: Keep thy servant also from presumptuous sins: let them not reign over me: so shall I be upright, and made clean from much wickedness.
19.14: Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of mine heart be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord my strength, and my redeemer.

20.1: The Lord hear thee in the day of trouble: the Name of the God of Jacob defend thee:
20.2: Send thee help from the Sanctuary, and strengthen thee out of Zion.
20.3: Let him remember all thine offerings, and turn thy burnt offerings into ashes. Selah.
20.4: And grant thee according to thine heart, and fulfill all thy purpose:
20.5: That we may rejoice in thy salvation, and set up the banner in the Name of our God, when the Lord shall perform all thy petitions.
20.6: Now know I that the Lord will help his anointed, and will hear him from his Sanctuary, by the mighty help of his right hand.
20.7: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the Name of the Lord our God.
20.8: They are brought down and fallen, but we are risen, and stand upright.
20.9: Save Lord: Let the King hear us in the day that we call.

21.1: The King shall rejoice in thy strength, O Lord: yea how greatly shall he rejoice in thy salvation?
21.2: Thou hast given him his heart’s desire, and hast not denied him the request of his lips. Selah.
21.3: For thou didst prevent him with liberal blessings, and didst set a crown of pure gold upon his head.
21.4: He asked life of thee, and thou gavest him a long life forever and ever.
21.5: His glory is great in thy salvation: dignity and honor hast thou laid upon him.
21.6: For thou hast set him as blessings forever: thou hast made him glad with the joy of thy countenance.
21.7: Because the king trusteth in the Lord, and in the mercy of the most high, he shall not slide.
21.8: Thine hand shall find out all thine enemies, and thy right hand shall find out them that hate thee.
21.9: Thou shalt make them like a fiery oven in time of thine anger: the Lord shall destroy them in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them.
21.10: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from the children of men.
21.11: For they intended evil against thee, and imagined mischief, but they shall not prevail.
21.12: Therefore shalt thou put them apart, and the strings of thy bow shalt thou make ready against their faces.
21.13: Be thou exalted, O Lord, in thy strength: so will we sing and praise thy power.

22.1: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me, and art so far from mine health, and from the words of my roaring?
22.2: O my God, I cry by day, but thou hearest not: and by night, but have no audience.
22.3: But thou art holy, and dost inhabit the praises of Israel.
22.4: Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them.
22.5: They called upon thee, and were delivered: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.
22.6: But I am a worm, and not a man: a shame of men, and the contempt of the people.
22.7: All they that see me, have me in derision: they make a mow and nod the head, saying,
22.8: He trusted in the Lord, let him deliver him: let him save him, seeing he loveth him.
22.9: But thou didst draw me out of the womb: thou gavest me hope, even at my mother’s breasts.
22.10: I was cast upon thee, even from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.
22.11: Be not far from me, because trouble is near: for there is none to help me.
22.12: Many young bulls have compassed me: mighty bulls of Bashan have closed me about.
22.13: They gape upon me with their mouths, as a ramping and roaring lion.
22.14: I am like water poured out, and all my bones are out of joint: mine heart is like wax: it is molten in the midst of my bowels.
22.15: My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws, and thou hast brought me into the dust of death.
22.16: For dogs have compassed me, and the assembly of the wicked have enclosed me: they pierced mine hands and my feet.
22.17: I may tell all my bones, yet they behold, and look upon me.
22.18: They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.
22.19: But be not thou far off, O Lord, my strength: hasten to help me.
22.20: Deliver my soul from the sword: my desolate soul from the power of the dog.
22.21: Save me from the lion’s mouth, and answer me in saving me from the horns of the unicorns.
22.22: I will declare thy Name unto my brethren: in the midst of the Congregation will I praise thee, saying,
22.23: Praise the Lord, ye that fear him: magnify ye him, all the seed of Jacob, and fear ye him all the seed of Israel.
22.24: For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the poor: neither hath he hid his face from him, but when he called unto him, he heard.
22.25: My praise shall be of thee in the great Congregation: my vows will I perform before them that fear him.
22.26: The poor shall eat and be satisfied: they that seek after the Lord, shall praise him: your heart shall live forever.
22.27: All the ends of the world shall remember themselves and turn to the Lord, and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee.
22.28: For the kingdom is the Lord’s, and he ruleth among the nations.
22.29: All they that be fat in the earth shall eat and worship: all they that go down into the dust, shall bow before him, even he that cannot quicken his own soul.
22.30: Their seed shall serve him: it shall be counted unto the Lord for a generation.
22.31: They shall come and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born, because he hath done it.

23.1: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.
23.2: He maketh me to rest in green pasture, and leadeth me by the still waters.
23.3: He restoreth my soul, and leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his Name’s sake.
23.4: Yea, though I should walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil; for thou art with me: thy rod and thy staff, they comfort me.
23.5: Thou dost prepare a table before me in the sight of mine adversaries: thou dost anoint mine head with oil, and my cup runneth over.
23.6: Doubtless kindness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I shall remain a long season in the house of the Lord.

24.1: The earth is the Lord’s, and all that therein is; the world and they that dwell therein.
24.2: For he hath founded it upon the seas; and established it upon the floods.
24.3: Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord? and who shall stand in his holy place?
24.4: Even he that hath innocent hands, and a pure heart; which hath not lifted up his mind unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully.
24.5: He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.
24.6: This is the generation of them that seek him, of them that seek thy face, this is Jacob. Selah.
24.7: Lift up your heads ye gates, and be ye lifted up ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in.
24.8: Who is this King of glory? the Lord, strong and mighty, even the Lord mighty in battle.
24.9: Lift up your heads, ye gates, and lift up yourselves ye everlasting doors, and the King of glory shall come in.
24.10: Who is this King of glory? the Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory. Selah.

25.1: Unto thee, O Lord, lift I up my soul.
25.2: My God, I trust in thee; let me not be confounded: let not mine enemies rejoice over me.
25.3: So all that hope in thee, shall not be ashamed; but let them be confounded, that transgress without cause.
25.4: Show me thy ways, O Lord, and teach me thy paths.
25.5: Lead me forth in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation: in thee do I trust all the day.
25.6: Remember, O Lord, thy tender mercies, and thy lovingkindness: for they have been forever.
25.7: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my rebellions, but according to thy kindness remember thou me, even for thy goodness sake, O Lord.
25.8: Gracious and righteous is the Lord: therefore will he teach sinners in the way.
25.9: Them that be meek, will he guide in judgment, and teach the humble his way.
25.10: All the paths of the Lord are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies:
25.11: For thy Name’s sake, O Lord, be merciful unto mine iniquity, for it is great.
25.12: What man is he that feareth the Lord? him will he teach the way that he shall choose.
25.13: His soul shall dwell at ease, and his seed shall inherit the land.
25.14: The secret of the Lord is revealed to them that fear him: and his Covenant to give them understanding.
25.15: Mine eyes are ever toward the Lord: for he will bring my feet out of the net.
25.16: Turn thy face unto me, and have mercy upon me: for I am desolate and poor.
25.17: The sorrows of mine heart are enlarged: draw me out of my troubles.
25.18: Look upon mine affliction and my travail, and forgive all my sins.
25.19: Behold mine enemies, for they are many, and they hate me with cruel hatred.
25.20: Keep my soul and deliver me: let me not be confounded: for I trust in thee.
25.21: Let mine uprightness and equity preserve me; for mine hope is in thee.
25.22: Deliver Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.

26.1: Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in mine innocency: my trust hath been also in the Lord: therefore shall I not slide.
26.2: Prove me, O Lord, and try me: examine my reins, and mine heart.
26.3: For thy lovingkindness is before mine eyes: therefore have I walked in thy truth.
26.4: I have not haunted with vain persons, neither kept company with the dissemblers.
26.5: I have hated the assembly of the evil, and have not companied with the wicked.
26.6: I will wash mine hands in innocency, O Lord, and compass thine altar,
26.7: That I may declare with the voice of thanksgiving, and set forth all thy wondrous works.
26.8: O Lord, I have loved the habitation of thine house, and the place where thine honor dwelleth.
26.9: Gather not my soul with the sinners, nor my life with the bloody men:
26.10: In whose hand is wickedness, and their right hand is full of bribes.
26.11: But I will walk in mine innocency: redeem me therefore, and be merciful unto me.
26.12: My foot standeth in uprightness: I will praise thee, O Lord, in the Congregations.

27.1: The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear? the Lord is the strength of my life, of whom shall I be afraid?
27.2: When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell.
27.3: Though an host pitched against me, mine heart should not be afraid: though war be raised against me, I will trust in this.
27.4: One thing have I desired of the Lord, that I will require, even that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the Lord, and to visit his Temple.
27.5: For in the time of trouble he shall hide me in his Tabernacle: in the secret place of his pavilion shall he hide me, and set me up upon a rock.
27.6: And now shall he lift up mine head above mine enemies round about me: therefore will I offer in his Tabernacle sacrifices of joy: I will sing and praise the Lord.
27.7: Hearken unto my voice, O Lord, when I cry: have mercy also upon me and hear me.
27.8: When thou saidest, Seek ye my face, mine heart answered unto thee, O Lord, I will seek thy face.
27.9: Hide not therefore thy face from me, nor cast thy servant away in displeasure: thou hast been my succor, leave me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.
27.10: Though my father and my mother should forsake me, yet the Lord will gather me up.
27.11: Teach me thy way, O Lord, and lead me in a right path, because of mine enemies.
27.12: Give me not unto the lust of mine adversaries: for there are false witnesses risen up against me, and such as speak cruelly.
27.13: I should have fainted, except I had believed to see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.
27.14: Hope in the Lord: be strong, and he shall comfort thine heart, and trust in the Lord.

28.1: Unto thee, O Lord, do I cry: O my strength, be not deaf toward me, lest if thou answer me not, I be like them that go down into the pit.
28.2: Hear the voice of my petitions, when I cry unto thee, when I hold up my hands toward thine holy Oracle.
28.3: Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity: which speak friendly to their neighbors, when malice is in their hearts.
28.4: Reward them according to their deeds, and according to the wickedness of their inventions: recompense them after the work of their hands: render them their reward.
28.5: For they reward not the works of the Lord, nor the operation of his hands: therefore break them down, and build them not up.
28.6: Praised be the Lord, for he hath heard the voice of my petitions.
28.7: The Lord is my strength and my shield: mine heart trusted in him, and I was helped: therefore mine heart shall rejoice, and with my song will I praise him.
